announcements.text: RTX Corp., Pratt & Whitney, and Pratt & Whitney Military Engines, East Hartford, Connecticut, is awarded a $2,525,033,340 undefinitized contract action with cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost-plus-incentive-fee, cost, and fixed-price-incentive-fee contract line items for F135 propulsion-system sustainment supporting F-35 Lightning II aircraft (N0001926C0112). The effort provides global unit- and depot-level maintenance, repair, engineering, logistics, software sustainment, technical-data updates, support-equipment management, training, and replenishment spare parts. Work will be performed in East Hartford, Connecticut (40%); Oklahoma City, Oklahoma (21%); Indianapolis, Indiana (12%); West Palm Beach, Florida (6%); Windsor Locks, Connecticut (6%); Brekstad, Norway (4%); Leeuwarden, Netherlands (3%); Iwakuni, Japan (3%); Williamtown, Australia (2%); Cameri, Italy (1%); Marham, United Kingdom (1%); and Fort Worth, Texas (1%), and is expected to be completed in November 2027. Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Air Force) funds in the amount of $147,485,965; fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $33,905,531; fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $80,458,659; F-35 cooperative program partner funds in the amount of $99,431,792; and Foreign Military Sales funds in the amount of $75,383,115, will be obligated at the time of award. This contract was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Melbourne, Florida, is awarded a $1,130,397,498 cost-plus-incentive-fee modification (P00018) to a previously awarded contract (N0001925C0130) to exercise options for the design, development, and delivery of three E-130J system demonstration test articles and initial spares in support of engineering and manufacturing development. The E-130J program will integrate specialized, secure communications systems into government-furnished C-130J-30 aircraft to recapitalize the Navy’s Take Charge and Move Out strategic communications mission. Work will be performed in Melbourne, Florida (35%); Marietta, Georgia (23%); Richardson, Texas (15%); Largo, Florida (8%); Oklahoma City, Oklahoma (6%); Orlando, Florida (2%); Indianapolis, Indiana (2%); Phoenix, Arizona (1%); Torrance, California (1%); Clearwater, Florida (1%); Fort Wayne, Indiana (1%); San Antonio, Texas (1%); and various locations within the continental U.S. (4%), and is expected to be completed in January 2030. Fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $4,180,000 will be obligated at the time of award. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Raytheon Co., Tucson, Arizona, is awarded a $23,987,464 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification (P00011) to previously awarded contract (N0002425C5409). This modification exercises options for design agent and engineering support for the Standard Missile-6 (SM-6) weapon system. Work will be performed in Tucson, Arizona, and is expected to be completed in September 2028. Fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $13,213,914 will be obligated at the time of award. This modification was not competitively procured. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Amentum Services Inc., Chantilly, Virginia was awarded a $34,407,938 modification (P00120) to contract W58RGZ-25-C-0003# for aviation maintenance services to Combat Aviation Brigades. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $469,578,660. Work will be performed in Germany, Saudi Arabia, Honduras, Kuwait; Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland; Fort Campbell, Kentucky; Savannah, Georgia; Fort Belvoir, Virginia; Redstone Arsenal, Alabama; Groton, Connecticut; Kingston, Rhode Island; and Mariette, Georgia, with an estimated completion date of Nov. 30, 2027. Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance, Army funds in the amount of $24,895,713; aircraft procurement, Army funds in the amount of $400,170; research, development, test and evaluation, Army funds in the amount of $709,597; and Foreign Military Sales (Germany, Honduras, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia) funds in the amount of $8,402,459, were obligated at the time of the award. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Greenfield International Corp.,* Woodbridge, Virginia (W912QR-27-D-A002); Crico Enterprise LLC,* Louisville, Kentucky (W912QR-27-D-A001); Reliance Contractors,* Miami, Florida (W912QR-27-D-A003); Roku Management,* Henrico, Virginia (W912QR-27-D-A004); and Yenrub Consulting Group LLC,* McDonough, Georgia (W912QR-27-D-A005), will compete for each order of the $20,000,000 firm-fixed-price contract for janitorial services for all military recruiting offices throughout the states of Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, and Ohio. Bids were solicited via the internet with 23 received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of May 31, 2032. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville, Kentucky, is the contracting activity.

CORRECTION : The contract for Tenova Inc.,* Coraopolis, Pennsylvania (W519TC-27-C-A018), was announced on Nov. 20, 2026. The correct award date is Nov. 25, 2026. The contracting activity is Army Contracting Command, Rock Island Arsenal, Illinois.

Dell Federal Systems L.P, Round Rock, Texas, has been awarded a $10,000,000 firm-fixed-price contract for hardware warranty and monitoring support warranty, assurance, and telemetry for Cyber Hardware Defensive Operations – Global. This contract provides lifecycle sustainment, remote telemetry, service desk operations, cybersecurity compliance, and hardware warranty coverage. Work will be performed in San Antonio, Texas, and is expected to be completed by Nov. 22, 2027. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 procurement funds in the amount of $2,759,218; fiscal 2027 procurement funds in the amount of $2,882,779; and fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $4,358,002, are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Lifecycle Management Center, Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, is the contracting activity (FA8307-27-F-B001) (Awarded Nov. 20, 2026).
